html:
In January 1641 the Dutch East India Company and its ally Johor took Malacca from the Portuguese after a siege of about five months.

Malacca had been Portuguese since 1511 (see Portugal takes Malacca), and the walls of A Famosa held out until hunger and disease broke the defenders.

The Dutch did not make Malacca their centre: Batavia in Java was their capital, and Malacca became a second-rank port. It passed to Britain in 1824 and became one of the Straits Settlements.
sum: In January 1641 the Dutch East India Company and its ally Johor took Malacca from the Portuguese after a siege of about five months.
